completeness_argument: The walk executes exactly one of each priced row per visit: one incomplete affine addition (all field kernels and the a=-3 chord law, including the x1==x2 branch that aborts the step), one canonicalisation, one record append, one batch normalisation and one sort/detect share. Anything not in a row is not executed: the walk keeps no ring, no escape table and no coefficient state between steps beyond the 48-byte record. Peak memory is charged as a bound; it has no scalar coefficient under classical-group-work-v2.
normalization: protected p256-ecdlp C = 1000 scalar AArch64 instructions per reference unit; every row is an instruction count, no borrowed one-unit-per-addition price, no inversion multiplier.

price_sources.executed_count_route: WITHDRAWN. The instrumented kernels failed the instrumented-vs-plain equality control 0/1024 in v13, so no executed number enters any row here; only static spans and explicit formula counts are used.

fe_mul_ir.source: evidence/stepspans_core.json span fe_mul=147, TEXT-only nm span of the shipped p256 object sha256 96b736ef..., the same row v10p's accepted accounting used

inversion.derivation: Fermat chain for p-2: 256 squarings + 129 multiplications = 385 fe_mul, so I = 385*147 = 56595 Ir per inversion (v10p accepted row). No M_insn multiplier is used; it is a chain length.

record.address_basis: records are radix-sorted on the full 256-bit class key and compared adjacently; no 64-bit bucket mix is used, so the lookup addresses the whole key instead of a 2^64 prefix.

success.basis: birthday over the full store: lambda = V^2/r with V visits and r ~ 2^256; the coefficient-trivial 4-cycle channel removes <=2^-34 of the visits (evidence/cycle_channel.json).
